answer: For a meadow-to-karst watershed council, I propose a 24-hour voting horizon. Each key must upload 2 GiB of random test data to an appointed bandwidth auditor. The auditor signs a key/day receipt only after receiving all bytes; no transfer can count for two keys. Validators check signatures and key/day bindings; missing or invalid receipts mean no vote. Thus n identities consume 2n GiB of uplink daily, even if they share a connection. This ties up capacity, not unique humans. Colluding auditors can fake receipts; spare bandwidth and bulk discounts make attacks cheaper.
